cultures.name: Greek
cultures.description: Gods, heroes, and cosmic origins in ancient Greek traditions.
cultures.primarySources: Hesiod, Homer, Homeric Hymns; traditions differ across authors.

cultures.name: Norse
cultures.description: Stories of the Æsir, Vanir, giants, fate, and Ragnarök.

cultures.name: Egyptian
cultures.description: Deities associated with kingship, the afterlife, and cosmic order.
cultures.primarySources: Pyramid Texts; Coffin Texts; Book of the Dead; Contendings of Horus and Seth.

cultures.name: Hindu
cultures.description: Diverse interrelated narratives from Hindu religious and literary traditions.
cultures.primarySources: Rig Veda; Ramayana; Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana; Shiva Purana.

cultures.name: Mesopotamian
cultures.description: Deities, kings, creation narratives, and journeys to the underworld.
cultures.primarySources: Epic of Gilgamesh; Enuma Elish; Descent of Inanna; Atrahasis.

cultures.name: Japanese Shinto
cultures.description: Kami, sacred places, creation, and divine ancestry.
cultures.primarySources: Kojiki; Nihon Shoki; multiple variant accounts.

cultures.name: Yoruba
cultures.region: Present-day southwestern Nigeria and neighboring West Africa
cultures.period: Living Yoruba oral and religious traditions
cultures.description: Orisha narratives transmitted through diverse oral traditions.
cultures.primarySources: Ifá literary corpus (odù); Yoruba oral traditions; details vary by lineage and region.

cultures.name: K’iche’ Maya
cultures.period: Maya traditions recorded in the colonial period
cultures.description: Origins, creation attempts, and the Hero Twins’ underworld journey.
cultures.primarySources: Popol Vuh (K’iche’ Maya narrative; recorded in the colonial period).

characters.name: Zeus
characters.description: Ruler of the Olympians, wielder of thunderbolts, and guardian of oaths.

characters.name: Hera
characters.description: Queen of the Olympians, associated with marriage and royal authority.

characters.name: Athena
characters.description: Patron of Athens, renowned for wisdom, craftsmanship, and strategy.

characters.name: Demeter
characters.description: Goddess of grain and cultivation; mother of Persephone.

characters.name: Persephone
characters.description: Daughter of Demeter and queen of the underworld in prominent traditions.

characters.name: Hades
characters.description: Ruler of the realm of the dead, distinct from the personification of death.

characters.name: Odysseus
characters.description: King of Ithaca whose long return home anchors the Odyssey.

characters.name: Odin
characters.description: One-eyed god associated with knowledge, poetry, and slain warriors.

characters.name: Thor
characters.description: Hammer-bearing protector who confronts giants and the world serpent.

characters.name: Loki
characters.description: Clever and disruptive figure whose actions both aid and endanger gods.

characters.name: Baldr
characters.description: Beloved god whose death is a pivotal event in Norse myth.

characters.name: Frigg
characters.description: Goddess and mother of Baldr in the Eddic account.

characters.name: Jörmungandr
characters.description: World serpent who encircles the earth and opposes Thor.

characters.name: Fenrir
characters.description: Mighty wolf whose binding and release feature in Ragnarök traditions.

characters.name: Ra
characters.description: Solar deity who travels across the sky and through the night.

characters.name: Osiris
characters.description: Lord of the dead, linked with resurrection and judgment.

characters.name: Isis
characters.description: Powerful goddess who protects Horus and restores Osiris in many accounts.

characters.name: Horus
characters.description: Falcon-associated god who contests Seth for legitimate kingship.

characters.name: Seth
characters.description: Ambivalent god of the desert and storms, rival of Horus.

characters.name: Anubis
characters.description: Jackal-associated guardian of burial and funerary transitions.

characters.name: Vishnu
characters.description: Deity associated with sustaining cosmic order and multiple avatars.

characters.name: Krishna
characters.description: Central figure in the Mahabharata and Bhagavata Purana; widely revered as an avatar of Vishnu.

characters.name: Arjuna
characters.description: Pandava warrior who receives Krishna’s teaching in the Bhagavad Gita.

characters.name: Rama
characters.description: Prince of Ayodhya and central hero of the Ramayana; revered as an avatar of Vishnu.

characters.name: Sita
characters.description: Central figure of the Ramayana, celebrated for resilience and fidelity.

characters.name: Hanuman
characters.description: Devoted ally of Rama, known for extraordinary strength and courage.

characters.name: Ravana
characters.description: Powerful ruler of Lanka whose abduction of Sita drives the Ramayana.

characters.name: Gilgamesh
characters.description: Legendary king of Uruk who searches for understanding after loss.

characters.name: Enkidu
characters.description: Companion of Gilgamesh whose death transforms the king’s journey.

characters.name: Ishtar
characters.description: Akkadian goddess associated with love and warfare; related to Sumerian Inanna.

characters.name: Ereshkigal
characters.description: Queen of the underworld in Mesopotamian myth.

characters.name: Marduk
characters.description: Babylonian champion who defeats Tiamat in Enuma Elish.

characters.name: Tiamat
characters.description: Primordial sea figure opposed by Marduk in the Babylonian creation epic.

characters.name: Utnapishtim
characters.description: Flood survivor who recounts his story to Gilgamesh.

characters.name: Izanagi
characters.description: Creator kami who performs purification after visiting the land of the dead.

characters.name: Izanami
characters.description: Creator kami whose death and underworld encounter shape creation traditions.

characters.name: Amaterasu
characters.description: Sun kami whose withdrawal into a cave darkens the world.

characters.name: Susanoo
characters.description: Turbulent kami associated with storms and the slaying of Yamata no Orochi.

characters.name: Tsukuyomi
characters.description: Moon kami named in Japanese mythic chronicles.

characters.name: Yamata no Orochi
characters.description: Eight-headed serpent defeated by Susanoo.

characters.name: Ọbàtálá
characters.description: Orisha associated in many accounts with shaping human bodies.

characters.name: Ọ̀rúnmìlà
characters.description: Orisha closely associated with the Ifá divination system.

characters.name: Èṣù
characters.description: Messenger and mediator whose stories often explore perspective and consequence.

characters.name: Ògún
characters.description: Orisha connected with ironworking, tools, and paths.

characters.name: Ṣàngó
characters.description: Orisha of thunder and lightning, also linked with historical kingship.

characters.name: Ọ̀ṣun
characters.description: River orisha associated with fertility, care, and prosperity.

characters.name: Hunahpu
characters.description: One of the Hero Twins who challenge the lords of Xibalba.

characters.name: Xbalanque
characters.description: Hero Twin who joins Hunahpu in overcoming underworld trials.

characters.name: One Hunahpu
characters.description: Father of the Hero Twins whose fate motivates their underworld journey.

characters.name: Seven Hunahpu
characters.description: Brother of One Hunahpu, summoned to Xibalba in the Popol Vuh.

characters.name: One Death
characters.description: One of the principal lords of Xibalba in the Popol Vuh.

characters.name: Seven Death
characters.description: Underworld lord who participates in the twins’ trials.

characters.name: Heart of Sky
characters.description: Creator figure or designation invoked in the Popol Vuh creation narrative.

myths.title: Origins and Succession of the Gods
myths.summary: Hesiod recounts successive generations of divine power, culminating in Zeus establishing Olympian rule.
myths.textSource: Hesiod, Theogony

myths.title: Demeter and Persephone
myths.summary: After Persephone is taken to the underworld, Demeter withholds agricultural fertility until a negotiated return permits reunion for part of the year.
myths.textSource: Homeric Hymn to Demeter

myths.title: Odysseus and the Cyclops
myths.summary: Odysseus escapes Polyphemus through deception, but reveals his name and provokes further hardship.
myths.textSource: Homer, Odyssey, Book 9

myths.title: Birth of Athena
myths.summary: Athena emerges from Zeus in a striking account of divine birth and wisdom.
myths.textSource: Hesiod, Theogony; alternative accounts in later Greek sources

myths.title: Death of Baldr
myths.summary: Loki engineers the fatal mistletoe strike against Baldr, setting in motion grief and forebodings of the end times.
myths.textSource: Snorri Sturluson, Prose Edda, Gylfaginning

myths.title: Thor Fishes for the World Serpent
myths.summary: Thor hooks Jörmungandr while fishing at sea; versions differ over how the encounter ends.
myths.textSource: Poetic Edda, Hymiskviða; Prose Edda, Gylfaginning

myths.title: Ragnarök
myths.summary: Prophecies describe a cosmic battle and destruction followed by renewal; Odin confronts Fenrir and Thor faces the world serpent.
myths.textSource: Poetic Edda, Völuspá; Prose Edda, Gylfaginning

myths.title: Odin Seeks Wisdom
myths.summary: Odin sacrifices and endures ordeals to gain knowledge, as told in distinct Eddic passages.
myths.textSource: Poetic Edda, Hávamál; Prose Edda, Gylfaginning

myths.title: Osiris, Isis, and Restoration
myths.summary: Seth kills Osiris; Isis gathers and restores him, while their son Horus later seeks rightful kingship.
myths.textSource: Plutarch, On Isis and Osiris (late retelling); Egyptian funerary and temple traditions

myths.title: The Contendings of Horus and Seth
myths.summary: Horus and Seth dispute succession to Osiris and submit competing claims before a divine tribunal.
myths.textSource: The Contendings of Horus and Seth (Chester Beatty Papyrus I)

myths.title: Ra’s Night Journey
myths.summary: The sun god journeys through the underworld at night and returns with the dawn, renewing cosmic order.
myths.textSource: Amduat; Book of Gates (New Kingdom funerary texts)

myths.title: Weighing of the Heart
myths.summary: The deceased faces a judgment of the heart against the principle of maat in funerary depictions.
myths.textSource: Egyptian Book of the Dead, Spell 125

myths.title: Krishna Teaches Arjuna
myths.summary: On the battlefield, Krishna counsels Arjuna on duty, action, knowledge, and devotion.
myths.textSource: Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva (Bhagavad Gita)

myths.title: The Search for and Rescue of Sita
myths.summary: After Ravana abducts Sita, Rama forms alliances, aided by Hanuman, and leads a campaign to Lanka.
myths.textSource: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda–Yuddha Kanda

myths.title: Hanuman’s Journey to Lanka
myths.summary: Hanuman crosses the ocean, finds Sita, and returns with news after his mission in Lanka.
myths.textSource: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda

myths.title: Krishna’s Childhood Exploits
myths.summary: Stories celebrate Krishna’s playful childhood and extraordinary interventions in Vraja.
myths.textSource: Bhagavata Purana, Book 10

myths.title: Gilgamesh and Enkidu
myths.summary: A fierce encounter becomes friendship; Enkidu’s death compels Gilgamesh to confront mortality.
myths.textSource: Epic of Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian version

myths.title: Utnapishtim’s Flood Account
myths.summary: Utnapishtim tells Gilgamesh how he survived a catastrophic flood and received exceptional life.
myths.textSource: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet XI

myths.title: Inanna’s Descent to the Underworld
myths.summary: Inanna enters the realm ruled by Ereshkigal, undergoes stripping and judgment, and later returns under strict conditions.
myths.textSource: Sumerian composition, Inanna’s Descent to the Netherworld (Inanna is identified with Ishtar in later traditions)

myths.title: Marduk and Tiamat
myths.summary: Marduk defeats Tiamat and orders the cosmos in the Babylonian creation epic.
myths.textSource: Enuma Elish (Babylonian Epic of Creation)

myths.title: Creation of the Japanese Islands
myths.summary: Izanagi and Izanami stir the primordial sea and bring forth islands and kami.
myths.textSource: Kojiki, Book 1; Nihon Shoki, Age of the Gods

myths.title: Amaterasu and the Heavenly Rock Cave
myths.summary: After conflict with Susanoo, Amaterasu hides in a cave and darkness falls until the kami entice her out.
myths.textSource: Kojiki, Book 1; Nihon Shoki, Age of the Gods

myths.title: Susanoo Slays Yamata no Orochi
myths.summary: Susanoo overcomes an eight-headed serpent and discovers a remarkable sword in its tail.
myths.textSource: Kojiki, Book 1; Nihon Shoki, Age of the Gods

myths.title: Izanagi’s Purification
myths.summary: After visiting the realm of the dead, Izanagi purifies himself; major kami arise during the rite.
myths.textSource: Kojiki, Book 1

myths.title: Ọbàtálá and the Shaping of Humanity
myths.summary: In one family of Yoruba creation accounts, Ọbàtálá shapes human forms; roles and sequence vary across tellings.
myths.textSource: Yoruba oral creation narratives; variants within Ifá and regional traditions

myths.title: Èṣù and the Two-Sided Hat
myths.summary: A well-known teaching tale describes Èṣù provoking disagreement through observers’ differing perspectives.
myths.textSource: Yoruba oral teaching tale associated with Èṣù; versions vary

myths.title: Ọ̀rúnmìlà and Ifá Divination
myths.summary: Narratives within the Ifá corpus portray Ọ̀rúnmìlà as a source of guidance through divination and interpretation.
myths.textSource: Ifá literary corpus (odù); specific verses vary by tradition

myths.title: Ọ̀ṣun and the Completion of Creation
myths.summary: In a widely retold narrative, efforts to order the world fail until Ọ̀ṣun is included and her power acknowledged.
myths.textSource: Yoruba oral traditions concerning Ọ̀ṣun; details vary by teller

myths.title: Hero Twins Descend to Xibalba
myths.summary: Hunahpu and Xbalanque face deceptive tests and contests imposed by the lords of the underworld.
myths.textSource: Popol Vuh, Hero Twins cycle

myths.title: Fathers of the Hero Twins
myths.summary: One Hunahpu and Seven Hunahpu are summoned below after disturbing the lords of Xibalba with their ballgame.
myths.textSource: Popol Vuh, Hero Twins cycle

myths.title: Creation of the Maize People
myths.summary: After earlier attempts, creators form humans from maize, connecting humanity to the sustaining crop.
myths.textSource: Popol Vuh, creation narrative

myths.title: Victory of the Hero Twins
myths.summary: Through performance, transformation, and cunning, the Hero Twins defeat the chief lords of Xibalba.
myths.textSource: Popol Vuh, Hero Twins cycle

relationships.description: Zeus and Hera are spouses in Olympian genealogy.
Athena is a daughter of Zeus.
Demeter is Persephone’s mother.
Persephone becomes queen alongside Hades.
Zeus and Demeter belong to the same divine generation.
Odin is Thor’s father in Eddic genealogy.
Frigg is Baldr’s mother.
Odin is Baldr’s father.
Loki contrives Baldr’s death.
Thor and Jörmungandr confront one another.
Loki is Fenrir’s father in the Prose Edda.
Loki is Jörmungandr’s father in the Prose Edda.
Odin falls to Fenrir during Ragnarök.
Isis and Osiris are spouses in major Egyptian traditions.
Isis is the mother of Horus.
Osiris is the father of Horus.
Seth and Osiris are brothers in the Osiris cycle.
Horus and Seth contend for rule.
Anubis performs funerary functions associated with Osiris.
Krishna is revered as an avatar of Vishnu in many Vaishnava traditions.
Rama is widely revered as an avatar of Vishnu.
Krishna instructs Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita.
Rama and Sita are spouses in the Ramayana.
Hanuman serves Rama with devotion.
Ravana opposes Rama during the quest to rescue Sita.
Ravana abducts and confines Sita.
Gilgamesh and Enkidu become close companions.
Gilgamesh rejects Ishtar’s proposal, precipitating further conflict.
Gilgamesh visits Utnapishtim to ask about life and death.
Inanna/Ishtar and Ereshkigal are sisters in the descent narrative.
Marduk defeats Tiamat in Enuma Elish.
The creator kami are paired spouses.
Amaterasu arises during Izanagi’s purification in the Kojiki.
Susanoo arises during Izanagi’s purification in the Kojiki.
Amaterasu and Susanoo are siblings in the Kojiki.
Susanoo defeats Yamata no Orochi.
Tsukuyomi and Amaterasu are sibling kami.
Èṣù features as a messenger and mediator alongside Ọ̀rúnmìlà in Ifá contexts.
Both are associated with creation narratives; specific roles vary.
The two orisha appear in diverse ritual contexts; this does not specify a fixed genealogy.
Some Yoruba traditions associate Ṣàngó and Ọ̀ṣun; accounts differ.
Hunahpu and Xbalanque are the Hero Twins.
One Hunahpu is Hunahpu’s father.
One Hunahpu is Xbalanque’s father.
One Hunahpu and Seven Hunahpu are brothers.
Hunahpu confronts One Death in Xibalba.
Xbalanque challenges Seven Death among the underworld lords.
